reconcile.connective: Defenders read the oracle and its fulfilment as a sequence: Zedekiah did see the king of Babylon face to face at Riblah, and only then were his eyes put out, so he came to Babylon yet never saw it.

discrepancy.connective: The objection is pressed by Steve Wells in the Skeptics' Annotated Bible, who sets Jeremiah 34:3's promise that Zedekiah's eyes will behold the king of Babylon flatly against 2 Kings 25:7's report that his eyes were put out before he was carried there.

excerpts.excerpt_text: and thine eyes shall behold the eyes of the king of Babylon; and that was all; for they were quickly put out by him …
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly answers the exact pair: Zedekiah DID see the king's eyes (Jer 34:3 fulfilled) and was blinded immediately after (2 Kgs 25:7) — the sequence harmonization in the fewest words. Truncated before the next clause; ends with elision marker, not a fabricated period.

excerpts.excerpt_text: thus fulfilling the prophetic declarations, that his eyes should see the eyes of the king of Babylon, Jer 32:4; Jer 34:3; but Babylon he should not see, though he was to die there; Eze 12:13.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Names Jer 34:3 explicitly and draws the distinction the tension turns on — he saw the king of Babylon's eyes but did not see Babylon — treating both as fulfilled. One complete sentence ending on a real source period.

excerpts.excerpt_text: By this two prophecies that seemed to contradict one another were both fulfilled. … He was brought thither, but, his eyes being put out, he did not see it.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Explicitly frames the seeing/blinding puzzle as 'two prophecies that seemed to contradict one another' and resolves it — distinct voice naming the apparent contradiction. Two non-adjacent verbatim sentences joined by a sense-preserving ellipsis; both end on real source periods.

pd_work.note: Gill treats this exact pair at Jeremiah 34:3, granting that the oracle was fulfilled (Zedekiah did behold the king's eyes) and that his eyes were then quickly put out — the harmonizing tradition keyed to this passage. (Haley's specific coverage of this pair could not be confirmed, so a row-surfaced harmonizing commentator is used per spec.)
